correctness.rationale: For m≥2 loose hyperedges {hub,leaf2j-1,leaf2j} with whole-edge overwrite (fitness-proportional parent then uniform incident edge) and r>0, synchronized leaf pairs remain synchronized. The sole initially discordant petal for leaf seeding resolves before other type changes with mutant success rate r versus resident-leaf 1 and hub 1/m, giving c=mr/[m(r+1)+1]. On synchronized states (resident hub,k mutant petals) and (mutant hub,k mutant petals), genuine-change conditional probabilities yield u_k=bv_k+(1-b)u_{k-1}, v_k=av_{k+1}+(1-a)u_k, with a=r/(r+2m),b=2mr/(2mr+1). Boundary u_0=0,v_m=1 and geometric increment ratio q=(1-b)/a give H and exact hub/leaf/uniform fixation. Checked neutral r=1 directly and independently simplified exact m=2 suppression polynomial by symbolic rational factorization. Recomputed advantaged r>1 1/m coefficient and deleterious r<1 exponential scale via q=r^-2(1+(r-r^-1)/(2m)+O_r(m^-2)). Pointwise fixed r only; no extrapolation across r→1. All states can reach an absorbing consensus with positive probability, so finite harmonic solution valid.
residual_risks: No uniform error in a neighborhood of neutrality and no finite-m all-r suppression theorem for m>2.

value.rationale: Loose m-petal hyperstars form a canonical sparse linear 3-uniform hypergraph family and isolate group-overwrite versus ordinary graph replacement. The theorem gives exact hub-vs-leaf seeding, complete fixed-fitness large-size behavior, an explicit deleterious selection ratio and a sharp m=2 all-r suppression result. This is a motivated natural infinite-family classification, not an arbitrary sample of small hypergraphs.
residual_risks: Suppression for all m and all r is not proved; important nonuniformity near r=1 is retained.

limitations: Exactly loose m-petal triple hyperstars, m≥2, all r>0, model1 whole-edge overwrite.
